title: Other uptown drummers: Walter Brundy and Henry Zeno
summary: He remembers Walter Brundy as a reading drummer, does not recall John McMurray, and names Henry Zeno as his favourite, who played in Ellis' band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Were there any other good drummers up here uptown? Did you ever hear of Walder Brundy? Do you remember?
Yeah, I remember Walder Brundy. Well, see, during that time, Walder Brundy, he was up in Cantrell. Cant, Cant, Cant, out of the ground. Well, see, they were real drummers. They could read.
What about, say, John McMurray? Could he read?
Mac McMurray, I think they called him.
I could talk to him, but I don't remember. I don't remember him.
No, no, see, my drummer, again, was Henry Zeno. Yeah, he was a boy talking to him.
Was he one of the very best?
Yeah, he was a good one.
Who did he play with when you heard him? With... Huxley the band.
